claim_being_audited: That rejecting the vendor was policy-compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved control and quality-governance risk at the time of approval.
specific_concerns: The policy threshold is 'material unresolved risk,' but the summary does not clearly establish materiality beyond showing follow-up-worthy gaps.

The cited facts mostly support escalation or further diligence: informal quality process, an unresolved questionnaire inconsistency, and an analyst recommendation for follow-up if storage controls stayed unresolved.
The packet itself concedes the record supports unresolved risk more clearly than a reject-level control failure, which weakens the basis for a locked rejection decision.
Evidence access is limited to the actor's summary, so the support links between each cited item and the rejection decision cannot be independently checked.
One late quality artifact and mixed delivery history suggest caution, but the summary does not show that past performance alone rose to a material reject-level concern.
unsupported_claims: That the available admissible record clearly satisfies the policy requirement for a material unresolved risk warranting rejection rather than follow-up or escalation.
That the lower price was properly outweighed by documented, decision-grade evidence rather than by unresolved but still-developing diligence concerns.
evidence_requests: The underlying contents of BPROC-046-B through BPROC-046-E, especially the exact language describing the quality-process gap and storage-control inconsistency.
The approval record showing whether the storage-control variance was ultimately resolved, waived, or left open at decision time.
Any formal materiality assessment or procurement decision memo explaining why the unresolved issues justified rejection rather than conditional approval or escalation.
The past-performance record underlying BPROC-046-A, including whether the late quality artifact was isolated or part of a broader pattern.
Confirmation that no private or unlogged security-review results were relied on, directly or indirectly.
decision_criteria: Rejecting a vendor is compliant only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk.
Quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies can justify follow-up or escalation, but do not automatically prove a reject-level control failure.
The auditor should not infer stronger support than the record shows, especially where the actor's own summary describes the case as defensible but not strong.
Any reliance on private or unlogged security-review results would be noncompliant.
